completion_data.completion_summary: Removed the per-dispatch git-worktree isolation layer (dispatch-worktree.sh and its two test files) and unwired every caller across the source store; renamed and narrowed the build-heavy selection predicate to its one surviving co-scheduling call site; fixed the contention-manifest false negative; reconciled five affected test suites (all green); re-measured both byte-budget gates with honest numbers (SKILL.md 20,325 B, still 325 B over ceiling; eager-load unchanged at 67,980 B, confirmed untouchable by this task).

memory_candidates.content: When a test fixture needs two same-cycle candidates to both be admitted into one orchestrator dispatch cycle despite declaring overlapping file_scope paths, a plain concrete-vs-concrete overlap (identical path, or directory-prefix relationship) is structurally unreachable: orchestrate-batch-admit.sh's own pre-existing in-batch file_scope_collision check (scopes_overlap_first) unconditionally defers one of any two same-cycle candidates whose scopes are identical or in a directory relationship, before any downstream contention-accounting logic ever sees them. The only admission-invisible overlap is a GLOB entry on one side (scopes_overlap_first treats a glob-shaped string as an opaque literal and never expands it), which is also the one case a correctness fix might need to specifically target. Verify any new overlap-based fixture by actually running it in a sandboxed harness rather than assuming the shape works.

A background harness run started before a file edit lands can observe transient mid-edit state and produce a spurious failure (e.g. an unbound-variable error from a half-completed removal). Treat a baseline captured concurrently with ongoing edits as contaminated and not authoritative; re-run the full harness only after all edits for the unit of work are committed, and use that clean run as the comparison point instead.
